message:

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the actual order and refund data rather than rely only on W2's handoff message. Starting with the orders.
The orders are in, but W2's handoff only lists refunds. I should check the refund ledger directly before computing any net balances.

The refund ledger matches W2's handoff: orders 113 (acme) and 115 (cobalt) each have a refund, and both refunds are within their order amounts. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 22142 matches my own check: orders 110 and 113 total 29521, less the 7379 refund on order 113. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 49030 matches my check: orders 111 and 114 total 49030, with no refunds. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's net balance of 33952 matches my check: orders 112 and 115 total 40603, less the 6651 refund on order 115. All three balances reconcile with the order and refund data, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 22142 is recorded. Next I'll record birch's payout of 49030, which matches my own check of its orders with no refunds.
Birch's payout of 49030 is recorded. Cobalt is the last customer, and its net balance of 33952 reconciles with orders 112 and 115 less the 6651 refund, so I'll record that payout now.
All three payouts are recorded and each matched my own reconciliation from the orders and refunds. The batch is complete, so I'll finish with the report.
